key_insight: LoGeR enables dense 3D reconstruction over minutes-long video by processing streams in chunks and using a hybrid memory that preserves long-range context, avoiding quadratic attention and expensive post-optimization while maintaining high-fidelity reconstructions.
problem_solved: Scales feedforward geometric reconstruction to extremely long video sequences by overcoming quadratic attention costs and the limited effective memory of recurrent designs, eliminating the need for costly post-optimization steps.
method: Chunked bidirectional processing: split video into manageable chunks and apply strong bidirectional priors within each chunk for high-quality local reconstruction.
Hybrid memory architecture: combine short-term (intra-chunk) representations with a compact long-term memory bank to carry global scene context across many chunks without quadratic costs.
Cross-chunk retrieval & update: retrieve, fuse, and update memory summaries to maintain temporal coherence and dense geometry over minutes of footage in a feedforward pipeline.
impact: Makes practical, real-time-capable dense 3D reconstruction from minute-scale video streams feasible for applications like robotics, AR/VR, and large-scale mapping by reducing compute/memory bottlenecks and removing post-process optimization.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing: video stream → chunking → bidirectional chunk reconstructor → hybrid memory bank → merged long-term 3D output
Hybrid memory schematic: short-term per-chunk buffers + compact global memory with arrows for retrieval and update
Complexity/comparison chart: runtime/memory vs sequence length comparing LoGeR, full-attention, and recurrent baselines
Qualitative reconstructions: long-sequence 3D scenes (early, mid, late) showing consistent geometry without post-opt
paper_title: LoGeR: Long-Context Geometric Reconstruction with Hybrid Memory
paper_authors: Junyi Zhang, Charles Herrmann, Junhwa Hur, Chen Sun, Ming-Hsuan Yang
